Title: Magnitude 5 earthquake hits Tibet, hundreds of miles north of Himalayan flood
Article:
LHASA: A magnitude 5.0 earthquake struck China's Tibet region late on Thursday, the German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ) said.
The quake was at a depth of 10km in northern Tibet, GFZ said.
The epicentre was hundreds of miles north of the regions of Nepal and China that were hit by a devastating flash flood on Wednesday that killed hundreds and left more than 1,000 people missing.
China's earthquake networks centre also reported a magnitude 4.7 quake in Nagqu, Tibet, on Wednesday, state-run Xinhua news agency said.
China has activated a Level-IV flood response in Tibet amid the risk of a barrier lake breach, Xinhua added.
China's Ministry of Water Resources told local authorities to monitor the barrier lake and rainfall, and sent an expert team to Gyirong county, according to Xinhua. --REUTERS

Title: Nepal, China warn of fresh flood risks with lakes threatening to burst
Article:
TRISHULI, Nepal: Nepal and China both warned on Thursday of fresh risks of flooding in the Himalayas as two lakes that have developed on either side of their border threaten to burst in a region still grappling with this week's catastrophic flood.
Search and rescue operations are still underway in the debris-strewn valleys and hillsides, with nearly 1,000 people still missing after Wednesday's flood struck the border regions of Nepal and China's Tibet, killing at least 362 people.
Both countries have blamed the flood on a glacier collapse that pushed rock, ice, mud and debris into river systems in the mountains.
Nepal's disaster authority issued a notice on Thursday warning that a lake formed by debris blocking a river at the flood site is rising and at risk of bursting.
"Residents of the lower banks... passengers, rescuers engaged in rescue operations, and all concerned are requested to exercise special caution and stay in safe places away from the river banks and risky areas," the authority said.
China warned that 3 million cubic meters of water — the equivalent of about 1,200 Olympic swimming pools — are expected to flow into an already dammed lake on its side of the border over the next three days, creating a high risk of a breach, with peak flow expected around Sept 1.
The formation of a barrier lake was captured in aerial footage by a Chinese rescue team on Thursday, state broadcaster CGTN reported. The footage showed masses of brown water accumulating in a basin with no visible outlet. The water had already submerged bushes and trees and appeared to push against a barrier of debris and stones.
MORE RAIN EXPECTED
Rainfall forecast over the coming week will exacerbate the threat, Chinese state media said, citing the Chinese water resources ministry.
"The volume of water is continuing to increase, and so is the risk," Zhu Jinfeng, a researcher at the water resources ministry's hydrology department, told state broadcaster CCTV.
Heeding the warning, some rescue workers in Nepal began moving towards higher ground on Thursday.
Among them was Pawan Koirala, who began moving away from the river bed along with his team of 13 after the warning was issued.
"We are here for rescue and don't want to be near the danger zone," he said. --REUTERS

Title: The missing in Nepal-Tibet flash floods
Article:
KATHMANDU, Nepal: More than 1,400 people were missing and 362 were confirmed dead after flash floods and landslides hit the Nepal-Tibet border.
The figures are likely to change, which is not uncommon after a major disaster.
Double-counting of dual nationals, matching bodies with people listed as missing and the chaos of a calamity can all contribute to fluctuations both upwards and downwards in the figures.
Here is the latest on the missing:
- IN TOTAL: AT LEAST 1,468 -
Nepal's disaster agency said 910 people were unaccounted for on Thursday, a figure that included at least 517 foreigners. It did not give a breakdown of the nationalities of the foreigners.
Across the border with Tibet, China said 558 people – including 260 foreigners – were missing. Together, the the total missing on both sides of the border is 1,468.
Nepal's tourism board on Thursday put the number of missing tourists and travellers – Nepali and foreign – at 667 in total. Its further breakdown of the nationalities is included below.
- NEPAL -
The new Nepal Tourism Board figures Thursday said that 127 Nepali visitors were among the 667 it listed as missing.
It was not immediately clear how many Nepali residents of the area were unaccounted for.
- CHINA -
China's foreign ministry said nearly 100 Chinese nationals were among the missing in Nepal. The Nepal Tourism Board said 24 Chinese were unaccounted for.
That was in addition to the 558, including 260 foreigners, missing on its side of the border.
- INDIA -
Nepal's new tourism board figures Thursday showed 178 people from India were missing. Eleven others had been rescued.
- UNITED STATES -
Ninety US citizens were missing, the State Department said, adding that three had been rescued and it was not aware of any US fatalities. The Nepal Tourism Board put the figure at 65 unaccounted for earlier Thursday.
- UKRAINE -
Ukraine's foreign ministry cited Nepali officials as saying 55 Ukrainian nationals were missing. The Nepal Tourism Board put the figure at 53.
- MALAYSIA -
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Thursday that more than 50 Malaysians in Nepal are unreachable.
The Nepal Tourism Board put the number at 51.
- AUSTRALIA -
Thirty-four Australians are missing following the floods, said Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, though the Nepal Tourism Board put the figure at 35.
- UNITED KINGDOM -
Thirty-three people from the United Kingdom were missing, the Nepal Tourism Board figures showed Thursday.
- CANADA -
Twenty-five Canadians were among the missing, the tourism board figures showed Thursday.
- SOUTH KOREA -
South Korea's foreign ministry said Wednesday that nine hydropower workers were out of contact in the Rasuwa district following the floods. The Nepal Tourism Board said Thursday that four South Koreans had been rescued.
- SINGAPORE -
Nine Singaporeans were unaccounted for, the Nepal Tourism Board said.
- GERMANY -
Eight German citizens are missing, according to the Nepal Tourism Board.

Title: Ratko Mladic: Serb crusader dubbed 'epitome of evil'
Article:
RATKO Mladic, the so-called "butcher of Bosnia" who has reportedly died at the age of either 83 or 84, had insisted he was chosen by "fate" to defend the Serb people from a Western onslaught.
But he spent his last years in jail for genocide after he was convicted in 2017 for war crimes in Bosnia that the tribunal said at the time were "amongst the most heinous known to humankind."
The most notorious was the massacre of some 8,000 Muslim boys and men in Srebrenica in 1995 – a genocide, the court decided, orchestrated by military leader Mladic and his political comrade Radovan Karadzic.
The slaughter – the worst single atrocity in Europe since World War II – led media across the world to dub him "the butcher of Bosnia."
Former UN rights chief Zeid Ra'ad al Hussein described him as "the epitome of evil" after his conviction.
But most Serbs continued to revere him.
"He only defended his people," Bosnian Serb veteran Ljubo Tomovic told AFP.
"To convict him would be a disgrace and a sin," he said before Mladic's 2021 verdict.
Serbian state broadcaster RTS reported Mladic's death on Thursday after he suffered several strokes in recent months.
He pushed the image of himself as "a simple man" chosen to protect his people.
"Fate put me in a position to defend my country that you Western powers had devastated with the help of the Vatican and the Western mafia," he told his appeal hearing in 2020.
[[nid:1520263]]
Yet he oversaw a siege of the Bosnian capital, Sarajevo, for more than three years, his snipers and artillery shells killing thousands of men, women and children in the streets and in their homes.
And video footage from Srebrenica shows him reassuring a 12-year-old Muslim boy shortly before his soldiers massacre thousands of civilians.
At roughly the same time, he is seen returning to a deserted Srebrenica, telling the camera: "We give this town to the Serb people as a gift."
Mladic formed a Serb nationalist triumvirate with Karadzic and ex-Yugoslav president Slobodan Milosevic that unleashed a wave of ethnic killing in a bid to redraw the map of the region.
While Karadzic was the ideologue and Milosevic the wily politician, Mladic was the soldier and his metier was waging war.
Mladic had barely drawn breath before his life was indelibly marked by conflict.
He was born during World War II in Kalinovik in eastern Bosnia – most accounts say in 1942, but Mladic told the tribunal he was actually born in 1943.
His father was killed at the bitter end of the war, fighting for Marshal Tito, the leader who managed to knit together the multi-ethnic state of Yugoslavia and suppress simmering enmities.
By most accounts, Mladic always wanted to be a soldier.
He left for army training in Belgrade in the early 1960s, becoming an officer by the age of 22 and ascending to be commander of the Bosnian Serb forces in the war.
Although he was revered by his men, former Yugoslav army spokesman Ljubodrag Stojadinovic once described him as "narcissistic, conceited, vain and arrogant."
During the war, he baffled international negotiators with rambling diatribes on Serbian history.
[[nid:1520262]]
In the closing days of the war, close allies questioned his mental faculties.
"I respected General Mladic as a soldier and a man," the late former Montenegrin president Momir Bulatovic told a 1990s BBC documentary.
"But after three years of war, he'd lost contact with reality."
Mladic was dismissed from his post after being indicted in 1995, but he evaded capture for another 16 years.
At first, he led a life of luxury, pampered by the Serbian military, but the pressure on him mounted after Milosevic fell from power in 2000.
He was finally arrested in May 2011 at his cousin's country house in northern Serbia.
His daughter Ana killed herself in 1994 at the age of 23 with some accounts saying she could not bear the shame of the crimes committed by her father, though Mladic's family dispute this.
His last request before being transferred to the court was to visit her grave.
During all this time, his reputation grew, his wartime leadership immortalised in murals around Republika Srpska – the Serbian entity within Bosnia.
"I think that this verdict propelled general Mladic straight into a legend," said Republika Srpska leader Milorad Dodik after his life sentence was upheld.
"Serbs know that without him our people would have suffered much more."
Others disagree.
"Wherever their army came, wherever their boot stepped in, they committed genocide," said Munira Subasic, president of one of the Mothers of Srebrenica associations.
* The article is by AFP

Title: Death toll nears 400, rescuers search for 1,400 missing after Nepal-Tibet floods
Article:
BIDUR, Nepal: Rescue teams waded through mud on Thursday searching for more than 1,400 people missing after flash floods and landslides struck the Nepal-Tibet border, as the death toll rose again to 392, with entire villages swept away.
Experts warned of the risk of further floods a day after the devastating tsunami-like wall of freezing water and mud wiped out towns under a torrent of sludge, engulfing homes, smashing bridges and dams, and sweeping vehicles away like toys.
Many of the missing are foreign tourists, including trekkers in the Himalayan nation, as well as scores of Hindu pilgrims to Tibet's sacred snow-capped Mount Kailash.
The US Geological Survey (USGS) said the disaster was caused by a glacial collapse that triggered a vast flow of icy debris.
Climate change is causing glaciers to melt worldwide, increasing the risks of glacial lake floods and glacial collapses.
Emergency teams were racing to pluck survivors from affected zones, while Nepali soldiers used sniffer dogs to search for bodies buried under the suffocating dirt.
"It is a giant graveyard," Omkar Joshi, a 35-year-old Nepali customs agent rescued from a hilltop in the border town of Timure, told AFP. "All that is left are sand and pebbles, soaked red by human blood."
Nepali police said they had recovered 389 bodies.
Another 910 people, including 517 foreign tourists, were out of contact in the country. Beijing said 100 Chinese citizens – not accounted for in that tally – are also missing in Nepal.
Indians make up the largest number of missing foreigners, while the United States said 90 of its citizens were out of contact.
In China, state media said the "mudslide disaster" at the Gyirong Port in Tibet killed three people, while 558 people, including 260 foreigners, are missing.
Chinese Premier Li Qiang visited the area on Thursday, state media said, to oversee relief work.
China's Tibet Autonomous Region is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists.
- 'INLAND TSUNAMI' -
Prime Minister Balendra Shah, who urged the nation to "stand together" hours after the disaster, toured some of the hardest-hit areas on Thursday.
Shah told local authorities to "provide immediate relief to displaced families" and to open blocked roads, his office said in a statement.
Other foreigners out of contact include citizens from Australia, Britain, Malaysia, the Netherlands, Portugal, South Africa and South Korea, Nepal's tourism board said.
The sudden rush of mud and debris was "like an inland tsunami", travelling nearly 170km south into Nepal, said environmental historian Ruth Gamble, of Australia's La Trobe University.
Buddhist spiritual leader the Dalai Lama, who lives in exile in India, said he would "pray for all those who have lost their lives."
Chinese government officials in Tibet mobilised nearly 800 emergency workers, as well as sniffer dogs and speed boats to help the rescue efforts, the official Xinhua news agency said.
Promises of aid and assistance began to trickle in soon after reports of the scale of the disaster.
- GLACIAL COLLAPSE -
The USGS said a glacial collapse caused seismic activity and had "catastrophic" downstream impacts in Nepal and Tibet.
"This event was initially reported as a magnitude 4.4 earthquake," it said, but the seismic recordings were analysed and it was found instead to be a "glacial collapse and debris flow."
Fears of more potential floods remain, with water trapped by the immense piles of debris blocking the valley.
"With a blockage still lodged upstream on the Nepal-China border river, authorities warn a second flood may occur," said Qianggong Zhang, head of climate and environmental risks at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development.
Kathmandu's Flood Forecasting Division issued a "special notice" on Thursday, warning of a growing lake behind debris left by the landslide and urging extreme caution.
Scores of Hindu devotees from across the world are among the hundreds missing on the border, Indian spiritual leader Sadhguru said on Thursday.
They were returning from a holy pilgrimage to Mount Kailash, on the Chinese side of the frontier, when they were caught in the floods at an immigration post.
"The entire group was there in the building," Sadhguru said in a video message to his millions of followers, weeping as he spoke from Tibet, with the anguished wails of other pilgrims heard in the background.
"This is a terrible and extraordinary event."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Meta settlement: The warning shot social media cannot ignore
Article:
WEDNESDAY'S  historic settlement between Meta and dozens of  states could be just the start of a wave that will ripple across the social media industry, putting TikTok, YouTube and Snap under pressure to make similar changes to their apps for teens.
Parts of the settlement hinge on whether those three companies, referred to as "Core Industry Members" in a legal filing, take similar action.
It's "the right path forward for our whole industry, but this framework will only work if all our peers join us", said Meta chief legal officer C.J. Mahoney.
California led a coalition of states that accused Meta of designing Instagram and Facebook to hook minors, harvest their data and deceive the public.
California and New York are leading a separate suit against TikTok.
"We've definitely had communications with TikTok around our suit and what we're seeking," said California Attorney-General Rob Bonta on a call with reporters on Wednesday, adding that states also have been in talks with other companies in the industry.
Hawaii Attorney-General Anne Lopez called for industry-wide changes as well.
"I hope that Snapchat, TikTok and YouTube will read the writing on the wall and enter into similar settlements," said Lopez.
It's unclear exactly how the settlement will be implemented, or how far-reaching it will be, but Bonta said he expected it to be implemented "over the coming months".
If Meta violates the terms, "we will be able to hold them in contempt of court", said Bonta.
Many experts agree that financial penalties are the least of Meta's concerns.
A US$17 billion fine is a small amount for a company that has a market value around US$1.5 trillion and annual revenue of about US$200 billion.
Investors also seemed unbothered; Meta's shares rose one per cent Wednesday.
The bigger risk for Meta and other social media companies is whether the deal opens the door for more legal settlements and product changes.
"There will be more settlements in other cases as well because this certainly sets a precedent," said Vanitha Swaminathan, a marketing professor at the University of Pittsburgh.
Social media companies have evaded certain types of suits in the United States due to free speech protections that shield them from liability.
However, state prosecutors in this case focused on Meta's business practices.
"This might be how we regulate social media in the future," said Vincent Joralemon, a legal expert at Berkeley. "Sue them, then have them make the platform changes on their own.
"This is a clever workaround for First Amendment protections that otherwise stymie social media regulations."
Bonta said it was telling that Meta decided to settle midway through testimony from Adam Mosseri, who oversees Instagram at Meta — and before chief executive officer Mark Zuckerberg was scheduled to take the stand.
Mosseri admitted in court on Tuesday that he touted safety tools for teens without disclosing low adoption rates from early testing several years ago.
"The trial did not go well for Meta," said Bonta.
Thousands of suits brought against social media companies over alleged harm to young people have been winding their way through various legal systems across the United States.
Earlier this year, Meta and YouTube were found liable for causing harm in a Los Angeles case and ordered to pay US$6 million to a young woman. They intend to appeal.

Title: Gaza's children: War has stolen everything, even play
Article:
THERE are few joys left for 10-year-old Ahmed Hamdouna, whose childhood has already been scarred by years of war and displacement in Gaza.
Now, what little reprieve he found playing with scraps of plastic and sticks has also been torn away, as Israel warns it will step up military operations in the territory if kites continue to land on the Israeli side of the border.
"My father stopped me from flying my kites because of the occupation's threats," said Ahmed, who has been displaced to Deir el-Balah in the central Gaza Strip.
"I felt heartbroken after spending so much time collecting sticks and nylon, only for the occupation to prevent us from playing with them," he said.
"We are just young children. They destroyed our home and our whole neighbourhood. What more do they want?"
Israel accuses Hamas of cynically using children and says the kites could pose a threat, years after a wave of incendiary kites and balloons sparked fires in Israeli farmland.
A series of kites have flown in recent days across the border into southern Israel, communities shaken by the Hamas-led attacks of Oct 7, 2023.
Hamas has denied responsibility. No explosives were detected but at least one kite had a political message on it.
On Wednesday, an official of the United States-led Board of Peace supervising the ceasefire plan in the territory said: "All militant activity in Gaza must stop, including the flying of kites."
"Israel, too, must comply with the ceasefire," the board official added.
Hamas spokesperson Hazem Qassem said the popular committees in Gaza's displacement camps were trying to prevent children from flying kites, over fears they could be targeted by the Israeli military.
Ahmed said he was now scared of playing, but couldn't understand why the Israeli military was "afraid of kites when they are just paper and string."
"I don't want to hurt anyone. I just want to play like children everywhere else," he said.
For Gaza's children, building kites was a simple way to find joy among the ruins of war.
"There are no toys here, no amusement parks, not even a football to play with.
"The kite is the only thing we can make with our own hands that makes us happy when we fly it in the sky," said 11-year-old Yamen al-Mubayyed, who has also been displaced to Deir el-Balah.
"My friends and I get together and make them using pieces of wood we collect from destroyed houses, along with paper and string.
"We glue them together using flour and water, then go to the sea to fly them," he said.
Yamen said even the buzz of Israeli surveillance drones didn't put him off flying his kites.
"It is the only thing that makes us feel that we children are alive and gives us a sense of freedom," he said.
Israel has kept up attacks in Gaza, saying it is targeting militants, despite a US-backed ceasefire which came into effect in October.
Israeli army chief Lieutenant General Eyal Zamir on Tuesday vowed to push on with demilitarising Gaza "using all necessary means".
For parents in Gaza, the once-harmless activity now carries immense worries.
Akram Abu Shurkh, 30, said he had forbidden his children from making kites but felt he had "killed the joy in their eyes" in doing so.
"These are children who do not understand military calculations. They only see it as a game and a way to release their energy.
"But I see death in the touch of the string and the flying of the kite," he said.
In southern Gaza, 34-year-old Umm Moaz Huwayla said her heart raced from worry every time her children went outside with their kites, but felt she couldn't stop them from playing.
"The occupation wants to kill the joy in their hearts," she said.
"They are not asking for much, only to live their childhood, even with a piece of string and a sheet of paper."

Title: Dialogue with religious scholars guides government efforts - Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Dialogue with religious scholars provides an opportunity for reflection to ensure government efforts are guided by knowledge, informed by advice and refined according to the needs of the Muslim community and the demands of the times, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
"For me, dialogues such as this are not merely meetings but opportunities for reflection, ensuring that every government effort is guided by knowledge, put right through advice and refined according to the needs of the Muslim community and the demands of the times," he said in a Facebook post today.
As part of a series of muzakarah held this afternoon in conjunction with the spirit of Maulidur Rasul, Anwar also met Sheikh Dr Muhyiddin Awwamah, representing Darul Hadis al-Awwamiyyah.
He said the series of discussions with religious scholars was held to seek advice, gain wisdom and hear their views on the development and future of Islam in Malaysia.
Sheikh Dr Muhyiddin is the son of prominent Islamic scholar and renowned hadith expert Al-'Allamah Sheikh Muhammad bin Awwamah.
"I also expressed my appreciation for several books written by his father - a gift that is not merely a collection of written pages, but an intellectual legacy connecting generations and continuing the chain of Islamic scholarly tradition," he said.
"May this meeting be a small path towards greater benefit, for religion continues to flourish when those in power are willing to listen to the voice of knowledge, and knowledge remains a guiding light for the Muslim community," he added.– BERNAMA

Title: NST Leader: E-commerce's RM161.8bil question: Who protects the buyer?
Article:
HERE'S a picture of the Malaysian e-commerce landscape: so huge and impactful, and a little shadowy, that the government is forced to regulate the platforms servicing 26 million  customers.
Here's how it's financially impactful — the projected market size this year is RM161.8 billion, up RM147.9 billion from 2025.
The gross merchandise value (GMV), the metric measuring  e-commerce size, activity and financial projections, stood at RM83.3 billion in 2025 — the amount customers spent on all platforms combined.  Platforms like Shopee and Lazada earn five to 10 per cent of that RM83.3 billion.
The bottom line: the bigger the GMV, the more the buyers, sellers and transactions.  GMV growth is also propelled by faster and cheaper  Internet  access, reinforced by 2.43 million small and medium enterprises that went online in 2024.
Now comes this nagging problem. The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has revealed that 1,964 complaints were lodged against e-commerce platforms between Jan 1, 2025, and Aug 25 this year.
The MCMC is  investigating 118 cases, mainly about defective electrical and electronic goods and  scams, and four cases on dubious halal certifications.
The rub is that the MCMC is forced to play catch-up with a burgeoning industry that  transformed the way Malaysians buy, sell and do business.
The last time the government formulated a major e-commerce legislation was the Electronic Commerce Act (ECA)  in 2006.
Today's mind-boggling platforms and business models such as  cross-border marketplaces, livestream selling, algorithm-driven recommendations and foreign sellers dealing directly with Malaysian consumers, have  outpaced the ECA.   That Malaysia has the legal and technical know-how to regulate e-commerce  is a given but the real issue is more complex: how not to strangle innovation and legitimate digital businesses, and coordinating multiple legal jurisdictions into a single enforcement arbiter.
Like brick-and-mortar businesses, the singular idea is consumer protection. Ensure product safety, authenticity and accurate labelling.
Stave off misleading claims and scams, and offer  meaningful avenues for redress.  Foreign players with huge financial reserves and digital clout have the penchant to exploit regulatory  loopholes.
The regulatory principle is simple: if e-commerce platforms covet access to  Malaysian consumers, they must adhere to Malaysian rules Enforcement should rely on platform obligations and economic sanctions rather than convenient Internet blocking.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Hotspots rise in Kalimantan as air quality worsens in 10 areas
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The number of hotspots in Kalimantan rose by 254 to 520 today, and those in Sumatra increased by 12 to 176, according to the ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC).
Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said clusters of hotspots in West Kalimantan are generating moderate-to-dense transboundary haze drifting north towards western Sarawak.
According to her, the situation has affected air quality in several parts of the country, with unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings recorded in 10 areas across Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, Putrajaya, Negri Sembilan, Kedah and Sarawak as of 7pm today.
Sri Aman and Serian in Sarawak recorded the highest API readings at 157, followed by Cheras at 156 and Johan Setia in Selangor at 153.
Other areas with unhealthy API readings were Nilai, Negeri Sembilan (138); Putrajaya and Shah Alam in Selangor (127 each); Batu Muda, Kuala Lumpur (114); Seremban in Negeri Sembilan (110); and Sungai Petani, Kedah (106).
Azuri Azizah said three hotspots had also been detected in Malaysia, one each in Terengganu, Johor and Sarawak, based on satellite imagery from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA)-20 analysed by the ASMC.
She said the ASMC's Regional Haze Map also showed dry conditions across much of southern ASEAN, with isolated to scattered hotspots detected in the region.
In response, she said the DOE has stepped up enforcement and daily patrols in areas at risk of open burning, as well as regular monitoring of API readings.
Azuri Azizah said the National Open Burning Action Plan and National Haze Action Plan have also been activated to coordinate government agencies' response to open burning and haze.
"This includes preparations by the National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) to activate the Disaster Management Committee if API readings remain above 150 for more than 24 hours, as well as measures such as suspending outdoor activities, closing schools, kindergartens and childcare centres, and conducting cloud seeding operations," she added.
Members of the public can check the latest API readings on the DOE's website or through the MyJAS EQMS app.

Title: Only Aminuddin has returned allocations in full - Negri Sembilan MB
Article:
SEREMBAN: Former Negri Sembilan menteri besar Datuk Seri Aminuddin Harun is the only former Pakatan Harapan (PH) state assemblyman to have returned in full the allocations he received, while some others have yet to do so, Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said.
He said several former PH assemblymen, including the coordinators for the Paroi and Labu state constituencies, had begun returning the allocations from June 30 but had not repaid the full amounts received.
"As far as the Menteri Besar's Office is concerned, they have been returning the allocations since June 30, but not in full. The amount I gave yesterday was an estimate of the allocations they received.
"Some have indeed returned the allocations, but not the full amount disbursed. Perhaps they have already used it for the people and other purposes - I do not know. Those who have not returned the full amount must provide an explanation and expenditure records," he told reporters here today.
He was speaking after presenting flags to the contingent head and managers for the Selangor 2026 Malaysia Para Games (Para Sukma), also attended by state Youth and Sports Action Committee chairman Datuk Mustapha Nagoor.
Ismail said the Menteri Besar's Office was reviewing records of allocations received by each former PH assemblyman to determine the actual outstanding amount, as the sums received differed from one representative to another.
"The letters to be sent will not be the same for everyone. Some may have to return the full amount, while others less, depending on the balance for each state constituency based on our records.
"The letters will be sent after the review process is completed," he said.
Yesterday, Ismail asked all former Negri Sembilan PH state assemblymen and state constituency coordinators to return allocations received for the July to September period within one month following the dissolution of the state assembly on June 5.
However, he said the state executive councillors at the time, including Aminuddin, remained ex-officio members until July 31 and were entitled to use allocations for that month.
Earlier today, Nilai assemblyman J. Arul Kumar said allocations disbursed before the dissolution of the state assembly had been used for the welfare of the people and not for political purposes.
The Negri Sembilan Dap chairman said all unspent balances had also been returned to the Menteri Besar's Office before July 10, together with financial reports for each state constituency.

Title: Two killed after SUV crashes moments after U-turn in Gua Musang
Article:
GUA MUSANG: Two men were killed in an accident along Jalan Gua Musang-Kuala Lipis, near Bukit Lanjut, here, this morning, moments after a Proton X70 made a U-turn.
Gua Musang district police chief Superintendent Sik Choon Foo said the accident occurred at 10.24am.
He said police personnel conducting routine checks at Km16 of the road had earlier spotted the SUV being driven suspiciously.
The patrol unit trailed the vehicle for an inspection after it made a U-turn towards Gua Musang town.
"Upon arriving at the scene, the driver of the Proton X70 is believed to have lost control, swerved into the opposing lane and sideswiped the rear of a Toyota Hilux," he said when contacted.
The SUV then skidded onto the road shoulder before crashing into a lamp post.
"One man died at the scene, while another succumbed to his injuries at the hospital," he said.
Sik said several other occupants of the Proton X70 were injured and receiving treatment at the same hospital.
The Toyota Hilux driver and police personnel involved in the incident were unharmed.
He said the case was being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
"We urge eyewitnesses or anyone with relevant information to come forward to assist with the investigation," he said.

Title: Two inmates flee Dengkil drug rehabilitation centre
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two inmates fled the National Anti-Drug Agency's (Nada) Dengkil National Drug Rehabilitation Centre (Puspen) in Sepang today.
Nada director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh said the two fled the rehabilitation centre before stealing a vehicle from a nearby village.
"The stolen vehicle was later found by Nada personnel in Beranang and handed over to police for further action," he said in a statement today.
He said Nada, in cooperation with police, was conducting an extensive operation to track down and arrest the two inmates.
Ruslin said an internal investigation had also been launched immediately to determine the cause of the incident, including whether there was any negligence or non-compliance with standard operating procedures.
"Nada will take stern action if any negligence is found among the staff involved," he said.
Members of the public with information on the whereabouts of the two inmates have been urged to contact the nearest Nada office or call the agency's TeleHello hotline at 1-800-22-2235 or 019-626

Title: [UPDATED] Man falls to death, wife and 2 kids murdered in Desa ParkCity
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A woman and her two children were found dead inside a condominium unit in Desa ParkCity here today, after her husband was found dead following a fall from the building.
City police chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said police received a report at about 3.32pm that a 48-year-old man had fallen from a residential building in Persiaran Residen.
He said police subsequently went to the man's home and, with the assistance of the Fire and Rescue Department, gained entry into the unit.
"Three people were found dead in separate rooms. They were the man's 47-year-old wife, their nine-year-old daughter and seven-year-old son," he said in a statement tonight.
Fadil said all three victims had severe injuries to their necks.
Police also recovered a knife believed to have been used in the incident.
He said the circumstances surrounding the deaths were still under investigation.
"The case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder and sudden death," he said.

Title: MetMalaysia DG: Haze likely to persist until National Day
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The nation will likely still experience hazy weather until the National Day on Aug 31, said Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) Director-General Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip.
He said such a forecast was made due to persistent fire hotspots in southern Sumatra and western Kalimantan, coupled with southwesterly winds heading towards Malaysia.
"Analysis of weather forecast models monitored by MetMalaysia shows that several areas in Malaysia remain at risk of experiencing hazy weather with reduced visibility from Aug 27 to 31 2026, due to the influence of southwesterly winds and a high number of persistent hotspots in southern Sumatra and western Kalimantan," he said in a statement tonight.
He added that Sarawak will be the worst hit with most districts likely to experience hazy conditions at an unhealthy level.
"Several districts also have the potential to reach the 'very unhealthy' level on Aug 30 and 31," he said.
In Sabah, hazy conditions are expected to begin from Aug 29, while in Peninsular Malaysia, high haze concentrations may potentially occur in Johor, Melaka, Negri Sembilan, Selangor, Kuala Lumpur, and Putrajaya until Aug 31.

Title: Soldier killed in crash two days after wedding
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Just two days after tying the knot, a 24-year-old soldier was killed in a road crash in Tampin, Negri Sembilan.
Soldier Muhammad Alif Ahmad Rozaini succumbed to his injuries yesterday following a collision involving his motorcycle and two cars on Tuesday.
His wife, Noor Azilah Hanim Mohd Tajuddin, 24, who he married on Aug 23, was also injured in the accident.
The victim's elder sister, Umminadhrah Ahmad Rozaini, 29, said the family was devastated by the sudden loss of the sixth of nine siblings.
"He was usually quiet, but during the wedding, he was unusually talkative and even delivered a speech.
"I will always remember him asking everyone to pray that their marriage would last until jannah (heaven).
"His voice trembled, and he wept during the solemnisation," she said when contacted today.
Umminadhrah said the newlyweds were on their way to a bank to finalise preparations for the groom's side reception, scheduled for Aug 30, when tragedy struck.
Noor Azilah, who suffered fractures to both arms and legs, was scheduled for surgery on her left leg today.
"She is deeply traumatised. We set up a video call so she could watch her husband's final rites and burial," Umminadhrah added, affirming that the family would continue to care for her.
Alif, who was based in Melaka, was laid to rest at the Kalumpang Muslim Cemetery in Selangor yesterday.

Title: TNB deliver resilient 1h 2026 performance, protecting the rakyat amid west asia volatility
Article:
TENAGA Nasional Bhd (TNB) maintained a resilient performance in the first half of the financial year ended June 30, 2026 (1H 2026), reaffirming its ability to deliver reliable and secure electricity, strengthening national energy security and advancing Malaysia's energy transition amid a dynamic global energy landscape.
Against the backdrop of global energy market volatility, increasing electricity demand and evolving energy transition requirements, TNB remained focused on maintaining operational excellence, supported by disciplined financial management and strategic execution of its integrated business model.
TNB President/Chief Executive Officer Datuk Ir Ts Shamsul Ahmad said the group's performance enabled it to continue investing in Malaysia's energy ecosystem while delivering value to its stakeholders.
"Our 1H 2026 performance enables us to continue investing in critical infrastructure that not only powers households and businesses, but also strengthens national energy security, accelerates energy transition, and ensures we continue delivering reliable and secure electricity while creating value for our customers, shareholders and the nation," he said.
RELIABLE AND SECURE ELECTRICITY FOR THE RAKYAT
TNB has also enhanced its capability to restore electricity supply more quickly and improve outage management, particularly during periods of high electricity demand and extreme weather. - File pic credit (TNB)
Global fuel prices continued to influence electricity generation costs during the period, resulting in adjustments under the Government's Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA) mechanism.
The AFA reflects changes in actual fuel costs and is implemented through a Government-approved mechanism to ensure transparency in managing fluctuations in fuel costs.
Since its introduction in July 2025 until April this year, electricity customers have received RM3.1 billion in rebates.
Amid volatility in global energy markets arising from the conflict in the West Asia, the Government also channelled an additional RM435 million from the Electricity Industry Fund (KWIE) from May 2026 to cushion the impact on customers.
While fuel prices remain largely influenced by global market conditions, TNB continued to focus on areas within its control, including improving operational efficiency, optimising generation performance and maintaining supply reliability.
The group invested RM5.6 billion in reliability-related projects during 1H 2026 to cater for demand growth, strengthen security of supply and accelerate the energy transition.
Investments in smart grid technologies, network automation and predictive maintenance have also enhanced TNB's ability to restore electricity supply more quickly and improve outage management, particularly during periods of high demand and extreme weather.
These efforts contributed to an improvement in the System Average Interruption Duration Index (SAIDI), which stood at 23.45 minutes.
TRANSITIONING MALAYSIA'S FUTURE ENERGY SYSTEM
The Energy Transition Conference 2026 brought together over 6,000 delegates from more than 60 countries and culminated in 15 strategic partnerships spanning renewable energy, grid development and regional connectivity.- File pic credit (TNB)
TNB is also accelerating strategic investments to strengthen the country's energy ecosystem and prepare for rising electricity demand driven by industrial electrification, AI-based industries and data centre investments.
One of the key milestones during the period was the commissioning of the 100-megawatt/400-megawatt-hour Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) Santong in Terengganu, recognised as Malaysia's first grid-connected, grid-forming BESS.
The group also collaborated with Petronas Gas Bhd to develop Regasification Terminal 3 in Lumut, Perak, enhancing long-term liquefied natural gas supply resilience and support reliable electricity generation.
TNB further accelerated the energy transition with the successful convening of the Energy Transition Conference 2026, which brought together over 6,000 delegates from more than 60 countries and culminated in 15 strategic partnerships spanning renewable energy, grid development and regional connectivity.
Meanwhile, the launch of the Energy Transition and Sustainability Academy (ETSA) aims to develop future-ready talent while strengthening collaboration between industry, academia and policymakers in delivering practical energy transition solutions.
CREATING LASTING VALUE FOR ALL
The My Brighter Green Initiative 2026 underscores the Group's commitment to environmental stewardship, through the planting of 40,000 forest and mangrove saplings nationwide throughout the year. - File pic credit (TNB)
Beyond its role in powering homes and businesses, TNB continued to invest in initiatives supporting communities and environmental sustainability.
The My Brighter Green Initiative 2026 underscores the Group's commitment to environmental stewardship through the planting of 40,000 forest and mangrove saplings nationwide throughout the year.
The initiative supports biodiversity conservation and climate resilience while encouraging community participation and supporting Malaysia's broader environmental sustainability agenda.
TNB also allocated RM109 million for corporate social responsibility initiatives during the period under review.
Of this, RM71.1 million was allocated to education support through Universiti Tenaga Nasional (UNITEN) and Yayasan Tenaga Nasional (YTN), benefiting 7,550 students and further reinforcing Malaysia's long-term human capital development.
Another RM5.4 million went towards sports development initiatives benefiting 42,420 athletes and enthusiasts, including national hockey programmes.
RM7.1 million was allocated to school engagement initiatives, including Ceria ke Sekolah and Sekolah Angkat, benefitting more than 200,000 pupils and 50 schools.
Meanwhile, RM16.3 million was allocated to community outreach and support initiatives, including disaster relief and Projek Mesra Rakyat, positively impacting more than 200,000 individuals.
TNB also allocated RM400,000 to community electrification initiatives, including the installation of solar systems, LED lighting and electrical rewiring, benefiting 3,600 people.
In addition, RM8.7 million in zakat wakalah was channelled to more than 50,000 asnaf beneficiaries.
SUSTAINABLE 1H 2026 PERFORMANCE
TNB continues to focus on areas within its control by improving operational efficiency, optimising generation performance and maintaining supply reliability. - File pic credit (TNB)
TNB's resilient operational performance translated into a healthy financial position, enabling the Group to continue investing in critical infrastructure while delivering returns to shareholders.
For 1H 2026, TNB recorded earnings of RM2.0 billion, supported by higher electricity sales, mainly contributed by the commercial sector, as well as improved operational profitability.
The group's performance also enabled its board of directors to declare an interim dividend of 25 sen per share, in line with its dividend policy.
The dividend payout amounts to RM1.5 billion, which will be paid out to TNB shareholders, with 64.1 per cent set to be distributed to government-linked investment companies, including the Employees Provident Fund, Khazanah Nasional Bhd, Permodalan Nasional Bhd, Kumpulan Wang Persaraan and Lembaga Tabung Haji.
"Subsequently, this directly goes back to millions of Malaysians, reflecting TNB's commitment
of delivering value while giving back to the nation," Shamsul said.
The group's financial resilience continues to provide a strong platform for sustained investments in grid modernisation, renewable energy integration, digitalisation and infrastructure expansion that support Malaysia's long-term energy security and economic development.
STANDING FIRM IN SERVING THE RAKYAT
Electricity demand is expected to continue growing, driven by industrial expansion, digitalisation, smart buildings, electric mobility and increasing investments in AI-driven industries and data centres.
Against this backdrop, TNB said it remained focused on its core responsibility of providing Malaysians with reliable, secure and accessible electricity while supporting the country's longer-term energy transition.
"TNB is committed to delivering long-term value not only for our shareholders, but more importantly for the rakyat, by ensuring that the energy transition strengthens Malaysia's economy, creates new opportunities and improves lives for generations to come," Shamsul said.

Title: Sultan of Pahang orders three-day mourning for elder sister
Article:
KUANTAN: The Sultan of Pahang, Al-Sultan Abdullah Ri'ayatuddin Al-Mustafa Billah Shah, has ordered the Pahang royal family to observe three days of mourning following the death of his elder sister, Tengku Puteri Seri Kemala Tengku Datuk Seri Aishah Almarhum Sultan Ahmad Shah.
Comptroller of the Royal Household of the Sultan of Pahang Maj Gen Datuk Mohamed Zahari Yahya said in a statement that the three-day mourning period would begin today and continue until Saturday.
He said members of the Pahang royal family are required to wear white during the mourning period, while male members are also required to wear a songkok wrapped with white cloth, adding that the family is also encouraged to hold tahlil and Yasin recitation sessions.
"The passing of the late Tengku Puteri is a great loss to the Pahang royal family, particularly to the Sultan of Pahang and Tengku Ampuan of Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah.
"The people of Pahang are also urged to recite Al-Fatihah and pray for Tengku Puteri's soul to be granted forgiveness and mercy, and to be placed in paradise," he said in a statement today.
Tengku Datuk Seri Aishah died at a hospital in Kuala Lumpur at 9.15pm on Wednesday and was laid to rest at the Royal Mausoleum in Pekan this afternoon.– BERNAMA

Title: Fadhlina directs probe over pupil's death after school run
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek has instructed the ministry's Integrity Unit to take action following the death of an 11-year-old student after a school run.
Fadhlina's call comes as the Kedah Education Department had launched an investigation into a complaint lodged by Nur Qaira Alisha Ahmad Ilwan's family.
"I have followed the passing of the late Nur Qaira Alisha Ahmad Ilwan with deep sorrow.
"I extend my heartfelt condolences to her parents and the entire family for this very heavy loss.
"I have also directed the Integrity Unit to take further action in accordance with existing regulations and laws, grounded in the principles of justice for all parties," she said in a Facebook post today.
The girl from Sekolah Kebangsaan Bukit Pak Kiau died on Aug 25, the state's Education Department said in an earlier Facebook post.
Fadhlina added that the ministry's current priority is to ensure that the bereaved family is provided with the necessary space and support as they cope with the loss.
"May the family of the late Nur Qaira Alisha be granted strength, patience, and perseverance during this very difficult time," Fadhlina added.

Title: Nepal floods: No official confirmation of M'sian casualties so far - Wisma Putra
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Foreign Ministry said it has not received any official confirmation of Malaysian casualties in the devastating flood in Nepal amid unverified information circulating on social media.
The ministry, widely known as Wisma Putra, said it is urgently seeking confirmation from the Nepalese authorities through the Embassy of Malaysia in Kathmandu.
"The ministry is aware of unverified information circulating on social media and through other unofficial sources regarding possible casualties involving Malaysian nationals following the floods in Rasuwa District, Nepal.
"At this stage, the Ministry has not received any official confirmation of Malaysian casualties," the ministry said in its media advisory on Thursday.
The ministry urged the public to refrain from speculating or sharing unverified information and requested the media not to publish or amplify such reports.
It said unverified information may cause unnecessary alarm and distress to the families involved, urging all parties to await official updates and respect the privacy of affected families.
The ministry noted that its operations room in Putrajaya has been operating since 12 pm Thursday to coordinate information and provide a direct channel of communication for Malaysians in the affected areas and their families.
Family members with relevant information, including full names, passport numbers, travel itineraries, last known locations and contactable telephone numbers, are urged to contact the ministry.
The Foreign Ministry's Operations Room can be reached by telephone at +603 8887 4570 or by email at dutyofficer@kln.gov.my.
"Family members may also provide the relevant details directly to the Embassy of Malaysia in Kathmandu via email at mwkathmandu@kln.gov.my, with a copy sent to the Ministry's Operations Room," it said.
The ministry said the Embassy of Malaysia in Kathmandu remains in close communication with the Nepalese authorities, search and rescue teams, the Nepal Tourism Board, travel agencies and major hospitals in Kathmandu to ascertain the safety and whereabouts of the Malaysian nationals involved.
Consular officers at the High Commission of Malaysia in New Delhi and the Embassy of Malaysia in Beijing have also been activated to assist these efforts through engagement with the relevant authorities in their respective countries.
The ministry strongly advised Malaysians residing in or travelling through Nepal, particularly those in or near the affected areas, to remain vigilant, prioritise their personal safety and adhere to all instructions issued by the local authorities.
Malaysians are also urged to register and regularly update their contact details via the e-Konsular portal at https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my.
"The ministry will continue to monitor developments and provide further updates as verified information becomes available," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nepal floods: Embassy tracking M'sians in Kathmandu hospitals
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu is in close contact with hospitals in the Nepalese capital to identify if there are Malaysians who have been brought for treatment following the massive floods that hit the country.
Charge d'Affaires ad interim of the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu Mohd Firdaus Azman said the move was taken following communication constraints with those in the affected areas.
"Given that communication constraints with them are currently affected, we are in close contact with hospitals, especially in Kathmandu, to identify if there are Malaysians who have been brought to Kathmandu for treatment," he said in an interview with RTM, today.
A total of 55 Malaysians who were reported to the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu have now failed to be contacted following the flooding and destruction caused by the overflow of the Bhote Koshi River in the Rasuwa district, Nepal, on Wednesday, according to the Foreign Ministry (Wisma Putra).
In a statement today, the ministry said the information was based on the latest developments received from family members, travel agencies and other relevant sources.
Mohd Firdaus said Nepalese authorities had mobilised search and rescue machinery with priority given to seriously injured victims to be taken to Kathmandu for treatment while lightly injured victims were being treated in the affected areas.
However, he said search and rescue operations were facing challenges as the road leading to the affected area was reported to have been severely damaged for 40 kilometres, making the area inaccessible by road.
He said the massive floods had also affected local residents as several towns along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli Rivers were destroyed.
In this regard, Mohd Firdaus advised Malaysians in Nepal to always comply with the authorities' instructions from time to time, while family members in Malaysia who were unable to contact their family members were asked to immediately contact the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu.– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 1,476 Myanmar refugees to be repatriated on Sept 29 – Home Ministry
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 1,476 out of 5,000 Myanmar refugees will be repatriated to their home country on Sept 29 under the first phase of the Voluntary Repatriation Programme implemented by the government through the Home Ministry.
The ministry said the individuals had been identified by the Government of the Republic of the Union of Myanmar through Diplomatic Note No. 649/47 01(2026), dated Aug 13.
"The date was agreed upon at a coordination meeting involving the Home Ministry, the Foreign Ministry, National Security Council (NSC) and Defence Ministry after taking into account logistical and coordination requirements, compared with the Myanmar government's original proposal of Aug 28 this year.
"The Madani Government, through Home Ministry, has finalised the first phase of the voluntary repatriation programme involving 5,000 eligible Myanmar refugees to their home country.
"The programme will be carried out safely and responsibly, in accordance with procedures mutually agreed upon with the Myanmar government," it said in a statement today.
Previously, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Myanmar had agreed to take back 5,000 of its nationals currently in Malaysia following diplomatic negotiations and strong relations between the two countries.
He said the move was an initial step towards addressing the issue while ensuring public order in Malaysia was maintained.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail also confirmed that the Rohingya were among the 5,000 refugees in the country who would be repatriated to Myanmar, but declined to disclose the timeframe for the process.
According to the ministry, the repatriation process will use two Myanmar Navy warships and a hospital ship.
It said that this year, 4,008 individuals, mainly Rohingya, would be channelled into the Refugee Registration Document (DPP) programme, while another 5,000 individuals would undergo a phased voluntary repatriation process to Myanmar.
"As of Aug 15, 2026, there were 10,388 Myanmar nationals held at Immigration detention depots.
"It must be stressed that this figure comprises all Myanmar nationals detained and should not be taken to mean that all of them are refugees," it said.
The ministry said the Immigration Department, in collaboration with the police, was currently conducting the DPP process to verify the identity, nationality, immigration status, refugee claims and security background of each individual.
"The registration process for the group is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of this year," it said.
It said the government's strategy in addressing the issue comprised two complementary approaches, including diplomatic negotiations with Myanmar to ensure the phased, orderly and responsible repatriation of its nationals.
"The second approach is to register and collect data on individuals claiming to be refugees and asylum seekers through the DPP programme, enabling the government to obtain comprehensive and accurate information on the whereabouts of these groups.
"The data can subsequently be used for monitoring, enforcement, management planning and an eventual resolution, including repatriation to their countries of origin when conditions permit," it said.
The ministry added that the repatriation effort required accurate and up-to-date data on the individuals involved, while registration under the DPP programme needed to be supported by a clear pathway towards a long-term solution.
It said this was to ensure the mechanism did not merely serve as a registration exercise, but formed part of a more comprehensive government approach to managing refugees and asylum seekers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Former Negri Sembilan PH assemblymen appeal against allocation repayment order
Article:
SEREMBAN: Former Pakatan Harapan (PH) assemblymen in Negri Sembilan have appealed to the state government to review its order for them to return allocations already spent on welfare and community assistance.
Opposition assemblyman representative J Arul Kumar said all the lawmakers concerned had already spent part of the allocations on assisting the public, with some having used the funds in full.
"We did not use the funds for personal or political purposes.
"They were all used for community activities, including contributions to individuals in need, non-governmental organisations, Islamic and non-Islamic religious institutions, schools and those facing health problems," he said at a press conference at the Seremban MP's service centre today.
It was reported yesterday that 17 PH assemblymen and two constituency coordinators from the previous Negri Sembilan government had been ordered to
return the allocations
they received for the July-to-September period following the dissolution of the state assembly on June 5.
Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim was quoted as saying the decision was made at the state executive council meeting yesterday following concerns raised over the approval of the allocations during a recent special state assembly sitting.
Arul Kumar, who is also the Nilai assemblyman, said it would be difficult to return the allocations, particularly given the amount involved.
He said the allocations were channelled quarterly rather than monthly.
Based on checks, he said all PH assemblymen and the two coordinators had submitted financial reports up to June 30 to the Menteri Besar's Office as instructed, while any remaining allocations had been returned before July 10.
He said the letter stated that all assemblymen could use the allocations received on June 4 until June 30.
"So, how are we supposed to return the money now? How can we return money that we have already spent on the people?" he said.
Arul Kumar said the decision on the allocations was made at the state executive council meeting, and the Menteri Besar himself had explained the matter during the recent special state assembly sitting.
He said the funds were not used for personal interests or political activities, but channelled to the people in the form of various assistance while the service centres were still operating.
Although the state assembly was dissolved on June 5, he said the service centres continued operating and there was still a need to assist the public, including processing aid applications made before the dissolution.
"The money had already been given to the people during the period when we were allowed to spend it. Now that we have been asked to return it, we do not know how to recover it from the recipients.
"If there was any balance, we returned it. But for money already given to the people, NGOs and religious institutions, how are we supposed to ask them to pay it back?" he said.
Arul Kumar said they hoped the state government would review the matter based on the financial reports that had been submitted.
He said he planned to meet Ismail soon to explain the matter.
"We complied with the Menteri Besar's Office's directive and returned whatever remained.
"I hope the Menteri Besar and exco members will review the matter because these allocations were not for personal benefit, but were used to help the people," he said.
Meanwhile, Bukit Kepayang assemblywoman Nicole Tan Lee Koon said the allocations came under VOT P50, with their disbursement at the discretion of the Menteri Besar's Office.
"When the government operates as a caretaker government, the Menteri Besar's Office can channel the allocations to former assemblymen to coordinate the respective areas. Welfare and the well-being of the people cannot stop even after the state assembly has been dissolved.
"All governance procedures were complied with, as recorded in the Hansard of the state assembly sitting on Aug 18," she said.

Title: Families await news of 26 Malaysians missing after Nepal-Tibet floods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: "We can only wait and hope that they are all safe."
That was the anxious plea of M Subra, 38, who is awaiting news of his father-in-law, V Krishnan, 74, after contact was lost with a group of 26 Malaysians travelling on a spiritual pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet following severe flooding along the Nepal-Tibet border yesterday.
Subra said his father-in-law and the other 25 participants were queuing to cross the Rasuwa-Gadhi border in Nepal when flooding was reported in the area at about 8.30am.
He said the families received the group's last photograph at about 8am yesterday, when they were still waiting to enter Tibet.
"We have tried contacting all 26 of them, but there has been no response.
"We also contacted the agent, hotel and those managing their trip, but no one had any information about their condition," he told Berita Harian.
Adding to the family's concern, Subra said they had been informed that about 40km of roads in the affected area had been damaged by the floods, forcing search and rescue operations to rely on helicopter assistance.
He said he was also trying to obtain further information from Wisma Putra.
"I also contacted the Malaysian Embassy in Kathmandu this morning and was told that as of 8.30am today, no Malaysians had been rescued or found.
"We also went to Wisma Putra to hand over the names of all the participants so that the consulate would know who was in the affected area," he said.
He said his father-in-law had joined a 14-day spiritual journey to Mount Kailash and was scheduled to return to Malaysia on Sept 6.
"This is only the fourth day. They were supposed to cross into Tibet before heading to Gyirong, from where they would continue their journey to Mount Kailash.
"The route there is difficult and the weather is cold, which is why we are extremely worried after losing contact with them following the floods," he said.
Meanwhile, a separate group of 56 Malaysians undertaking the Kailash Kora spiritual journey in Tibet has been confirmed safe and was not affected by the tragedy.
Group leader Datuk Mohanadas Nagappan said
they were currently in Tibet
and continuing their journey as planned.
"We are all safe and are currently in Tibet. We are grateful that our group and the route we took were not affected, and we are continuing our journey safely," he said.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has ordered relevant authorities to
immediately coordinate
assistance following the devastating floods in Nepal and India.
The directive comes amid concern over more than 50 Malaysian travellers in Nepal who have been unreachable by their families since the floods, which have left hundreds of locals and foreigners unaccounted for.

Title: Myanmar cleaner charged with offering RM1,400 bribe to cop
Article:
KOTA BARU: A Myanmar woman was charged in the Sessions Court here today with offering RM1,400 to a policeman to refrain from taking action against her over an alleged immigration offence in April.
Cleaner Thu Zar Myint pleaded not guilty to the charge before Judge Dazuki Ali.
The 41-year-old was accused of giving RM1,400 in cash to a policeman serving at Gua Musang district police station in April 2026.
The payment was allegedly made as an inducement for him not to take action against her, who was suspected of not having valid identification documents, as well as against her friend, who allegedly did not have an entry stamp into Malaysia.
She was charged under Section 16(b)(B) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act 2009.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Asmah Che Wan prosecuted, while the accused was represented by lawyer Shastidaran Sathaiseelan.
The court denied bail for the accused and fixed Sept 13 for mention of the case.

Title: 'Butcher of Bosnia' Ratko Mladic dead
Article:
BELGRADE: Ratko Mladic, the former Bosnian Serb military chief dubbed the "Butcher of Bosnia" for his role in the 1995 Srebrenica massacre, has died, Serbian state broadcaster RTS reported on Thursday.
Mladic, who had suffered several strokes in recent months, was serving a life sentence in The Hague for genocide, war crimes, and crimes against humanity after overseeing the Srebrenica slaughter, Europe's worst act of bloodshed since World War II.
Serbian state officials and Mladic's family had appealed for his release due to his failing health, but those calls were rejected by the Hague tribunal.
He was the military face of a brutal trio, led on the political side by ex-Yugoslav president Slobodan Milosevic and former Bosnian Serb leader Radovan Karadzic, as the former Yugoslavia descended into carnage after the fall of communism.
The 1992-1995 war left around 100,000 people dead and 2.2 million displaced.
The most infamous atrocity was committed in Srebrenica, where Serb forces under Mladic's command executed 8,000 Bosnian Muslim men and boys who had sought shelter in what was meant to be a UN-protected enclave.--AFP

Title: EP Manufacturing Q2 profit jumps 19-fold on Chinese carmaker partnerships
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: EP Manufacturing Bhd's net profit surged nearly 19-fold to RM5.15 million in the second quarter ended June 30, 2026, from RM277,000 a year earlier, driven by its automotive localisation partnerships with Chinese carmakers.
Revenue for the quarter rose to a 10-year high of RM212.68 million from RM127.7 million a year earlier.
For the first six months, net profit increased to RM6.7 million from RM1.05 million, while revenue climbed to RM372.87 million from RM253.23 million.
Chief executive officer Hamidon Abdullah said the performance reflected the strength of the company's operational execution and continued progress across its strategic growth initiatives.
"In Q2 FY26, we announced that automotive production volumes under our collaborations with Great Wall Motor, SAIC Motor Malaysia and XPeng have surpassed 1,000 vehicles per month.
"We expect further growth as new models enter production and exports ramp up across Asean and other international markets," he said.
Hamidon said the company had also secured new component programmes for upcoming Proton and Perodua models, which are expected to support further growth.
"We continue to work towards our vision for a one-stop automotive manufacturing hub capable of serving global automotive brands and supporting Malaysia's ambitions to become a leading regional centre for automotive production and exports," he said.
